subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The resolution of an electron microscope is greater than that of a light microscope because:
options: the specimen is stained more heavily
electrons have a longer wavelength than light
electrons have a much shorter wavelength than visible light
electrons travel more slowly than light
questions.explain: Resolution depends on wavelength; the very short wavelength of an electron beam allows much finer detail to be distinguished.

options: Binding to a receptor to form a transcription factor complex that switches on target genes
Binding to DNA polymerase to speed up replication
Methylating cytosine bases to silence genes
questions.explain: Oestrogen binds its receptor, and the complex acts as a transcription factor that initiates transcription of target genes.

questions.q: Which feature of the genetic code means each base is part of only one triplet?
questions.explain: In a non-overlapping code each base is read only once, belonging to a single codon.

questions.q: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) differs in function from RER in that the SER:
options: synthesises and transports lipids and steroids and stores calcium ions
questions.explain: The SER lacks ribosomes and is involved in lipid and steroid synthesis, plus calcium ion storage, rather than protein synthesis.

options: occurs in anaphase II between sister chromatids
involves exchange of alleles between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes at the chiasmata
reduces the chromosome number to haploid
questions.explain: In prophase I, non-sister chromatids of a homologous pair exchange equivalent sections at chiasmata, producing new allele combinations.

questions.q: A tRNA anticodon is 5'-UAC-3'. The mRNA codon it pairs with is:
questions.explain: Antiparallel complementary base pairing of anticodon 5'-UAC-3' gives codon 5'-GUA-3'.

questions.q: In eukaryotes, splicing of pre-mRNA involves:
options: Removal of exons and joining of introns
Addition of a poly-A tail only
Removal of introns and joining of exons
questions.explain: Splicing removes the non-coding introns and joins the exons together to produce mature mRNA.

questions.q: During gel electrophoresis of DNA fragments, the fragments move towards the anode (positive electrode) because:
options: DNA carries an overall positive charge
The phosphate groups give DNA an overall negative charge
Larger fragments are repelled by the gel
questions.explain: The phosphate backbone gives DNA a net negative charge, so fragments migrate towards the positive anode.

questions.q: During which stage of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles?
questions.explain: In anaphase the centromeres divide and spindle fibres pull the sister chromatids to opposite poles of the cell.

questions.q: A substitution mutation in a coding region may have no effect on the polypeptide produced. This is most likely because:
options: The degenerate nature of the code means the new codon may still code for the same amino acid
The mutation occurs in an intron only
questions.explain: Owing to degeneracy, an altered codon can still specify the same amino acid (a synonymous/silent mutation).

questions.q: A totipotent stem cell differs from a pluripotent stem cell because it can:
options: Differentiate into any cell type including extra-embryonic (placental) tissue
questions.explain: Totipotent cells can form all cell types of the organism plus extra-embryonic tissues, unlike pluripotent cells.

questions.q: In PCR, the temperature is raised to around 95 degrees C in order to:
options: Separate the two DNA strands by breaking hydrogen bonds
questions.explain: Denaturation at ~95 degrees C breaks the hydrogen bonds, separating the DNA into single strands.
